findings.title: gnn_type.py imports two GAT modules that do not exist; nothing imports
findings.quote:
from triton_tests.gat import GATConv
from models.triton_nn.mean_gnn import TritonMeanGNN
from models.triton_nn.gat import TritonGAT
findings.claim: The top of helpers/gnn_type.py imports `triton_tests.gat.GATConv` and `models.triton_nn.gat.TritonGAT`, but neither `triton_tests/gat.py` nor `models/triton_nn/gat.py` exists in the repo (a full-tree `find` and a `grep -rn 'class GATConv|class TritonGAT'` return nothing).
findings.concern: These are module-level imports, and helpers/arguments.py imports helpers.gnn_type, which main.py imports first — so every entrypoint raises ModuleNotFoundError before any experiment starts, and the GAT / TS-GAT results (Table 1 TS-GAT column, GAT baseline) have no runnable code.
findings.resolution: Add the missing triton_tests/gat.py and models/triton_nn/gat.py (the GAT / TritonGAT layers), or gate the imports so MEAN_GNN can run without them; confirm which commit produced the paper's numbers.
findings.reason: Lines 14-16 of helpers/gnn_type.py match the quote exactly; a find over the repo confirms neither triton_tests/gat.py nor models/triton_nn/gat.py exists (only triton_tests/test2d_mean.py and models/triton_nn/mean_gnn.py are present).

findings.title: DSS-Mean and TS-SGC/GCN/GCNII (Tables 5–6) are not implemented
findings.claim: GNNType only defines GAT and MEAN_GNN; a repo-wide grep finds no SGC, GCN, GCNII, or DSS aggregation anywhere, yet Table 5 reports DSS-Mean and Table 6 reports TS-SGC, TS-GCN and TS-GCNII.
findings.concern: The architectures behind Section G.3 (Table 5, 'necessity of triple-symmetry') and Section G.4 (Table 6, TS-GNN variants) are absent, so those ablation results cannot be reproduced from the repo.
findings.resolution: Provide the DSS-Mean, SGC, GCN and GCNII aggregation modules and their GNNType entries, or point to the branch/commit that contains them.
findings.reason: Lines 33-34 of helpers/gnn_type.py match the quote; GNNType has only GAT and MEAN_GNN, and a repo-wide grep for class SGC, GCN, GCNII, or DSS returns nothing.

findings.title: No way to train on a single non-cora graph (Table 2 / Table 5 setup)
findings.claim: The only single-graph training set is cora: `trainset1` returns `[DataSet.cora]`, and `inc_trainset` with train_size=1 uses TRAIN_MULTISETS[0]=[] → also `[cora]`. There is no CLI/enum path to train on a single graph other than cora.
findings.concern: Table 2 (pretraining-source sensitivity: cora / chameleon / roman-empire / wiki-cs) and Table 5 (trained on cora / roman-empire / chameleon / wiki-cs) require training on single non-cora graphs, which the shipped code cannot do without editing the source.
findings.resolution: Expose the single training graph as a CLI argument (or add the corresponding TrainTestSetup entries) so the Section G.1/G.3 experiments are reproducible.
findings.reason: Lines 29-36 of helpers/train_test_setup.py match the quote exactly; TRAIN_MULTISETS[0]=[] is confirmed at line 8, so train_size=1 also produces [cora].

findings.title: End-to-end MeanGNN/GAT and GraphAny baselines (3 of 5 Table 1 columns) not in repo
findings.claim: The only entrypoint builds and evaluates the TS-GNN (GFM). There is no code path for the three comparison columns in Table 1: the end-to-end MeanGNN baseline, the end-to-end GAT baseline, or GraphAny.
findings.concern: 3 of the 5 Table 1 columns (and the GraphAny curves in Figure 3 / Table 2) cannot be regenerated from this repo; GraphAny is an external repo, but the two end-to-end GNN baselines have no training script here.
findings.resolution: Add the end-to-end MeanGNN/GAT baseline scripts (or reference the exact external commands/repo used) so the full Table 1 comparison is reproducible.
findings.reason: Lines 4-10 of main.py match the quote; a find across the repo confirms main.py is the only file with `if __name__`, so no baseline entrypoint exists.

findings.title: No requirements file; ogb and scikit-learn imported but not in install instructions
findings.claim: The repo has no requirements.txt / environment.yml / setup.py / pyproject.toml (verified by `find`). The README install block (README.md:8-14) lists torch, torchvision/audio, torch_scatter/sparse/cluster/spline, torch-geometric, neptune, triton — but not `ogb` (imported here) or `scikit-learn` (used in transforms/pca.py, transforms/least_squares.py, helpers/split_data.py).
findings.concern: `import ogb` and `import sklearn` will fail on a clean environment built only from the README, and no pinned dependency manifest exists, so the environment cannot be rebuilt deterministically.
findings.resolution: Add a pinned requirements file including ogb and scikit-learn (and any other transitive deps) so the environment is reproducible.
findings.reason: Line 16 of helpers/datasets.py matches the quote; find confirms no requirements.txt, environment.yml, setup.py, or pyproject.toml exists in the repo.

findings.title: Fold index uses `seed % train_mask.ndim` (=2), so only 2 official splits ever used
findings.quote:
split_index = seed
# Avoid invalid split index
split_index = (split_index % train_mask.ndim)
findings.claim: For datasets whose official masks are 2-D `[N, num_splits]` (heterophilous, wiki-net, WebKB, texas, wiki-cs, …), the per-seed split column is `seed % train_mask.ndim`. `train_mask.ndim` is the number of tensor dimensions (always 2 for a 2-D mask), not the number of splits, so seeds 0..4 select columns [0,1,0,1,0].
findings.concern: The paper reports mean±std over five random seeds, but for every multi-split dataset only two distinct official splits (columns 0 and 1) are ever evaluated and three of them are duplicates, so the reported variability and the choice of splits do not match the intended '5 seeds' protocol. The obvious intent was `% train_mask.shape[1]` (num_splits).
findings.resolution: Change to `split_index = seed % train_mask.shape[1]` and re-run; confirm whether the reported numbers used the buggy indexing.
findings.reason: Lines 62-64 of helpers/split_data.py match the quote exactly; `train_mask.ndim` is the number of tensor dimensions (always 2 for a 2-D mask), not the number of splits, confirming the bug.

findings.title: align_masks folds test_mask into train_mask; test labels enter the label-prop input at eval
findings.quote:
train_mask = data.train_mask
test_mask = data.test_mask
if train_mask.ndim > test_mask.ndim:
    test_mask = test_mask.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(train_mask)
elif test_mask.ndim > train_mask.ndim:
    train_mask = train_mask.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(test_mask)
data.train_mask = train_mask | test_mask
findings.claim: For any dataset that ships train+test masks, align_masks sets train_mask = train_mask | test_mask (test nodes become members of train_mask), while test_mask is left unchanged. At evaluation, experiment.py:243-244 builds `train_y` = labels of all `train_mask` nodes, gfm.py:80 sets `lp_mask = train_mask` (is_batch=False) and propagates those labels; accuracy is then scored on `data.test_mask` (experiment.py:249,256) — i.e. the test nodes' own ground-truth labels are fed to the model that predicts them.
findings.concern: This is a leakage channel on the ~15 datasets with official splits (heterophilous, planetoid pubmed/citeseer, wiki-net, WebKB, texas, wiki-cs, arxiv): the evaluated test nodes have their true labels in the model's label input (and the LS/pool operators in transforms/least_squares.py:106-112,122-123 are fit on `data.train_mask` = train∪test), whereas the val split is excluded — so val and test are not evaluated under the same protocol. Because the headline Table 1 margin of TS-Mean over GraphAny is only ~0.2% (65.78 vs 65.56), even small leakage-driven inflation on the official-split datasets could account for the claimed advantage. (Ambiguity: the model is trained with target labels masked, so it is not explicitly trained to copy self-labels, and the reported per-dataset numbers on leaked datasets are not obviously ceiling-inflated — the magnitude is unverified without a GPU run.)
findings.resolution: At evaluation, exclude test (and val) nodes from the propagation input (`train_y`) and from the LS fit, matching GraphAny's protocol; re-run and report whether Table 1 changes. Clarify whether align_masks' union was intended.
findings.reason: Lines 86-92 of helpers/datasets.py match the quote; experiment.py:243-244 confirms train_y is built from train_mask nodes at eval time, and gfm.py:80 confirms lp_mask = train_mask in the is_batch=False eval path.

findings.title: Paper says 'official splits'; code generates 20/class splits when masks are absent
findings.quote:
else:
    n_nodes = data.x.shape[0]
    label = data.y
    num_class = label.max().item() + 1
    train_mask, val_mask, test_mask = graphany_mask_splits(
        n_nodes, label, num_train_nodes=20 * num_class, seed=seed
    )
findings.claim: When a dataset's PyG loader does not provide train/val/test masks (e.g. Amazon computers/photo, Coauthor co-cs/co-physics, Airports brazil/usa/europe, CitationFull full-cora/full-DBLP, AttributedGraph wiki-attr/blogcatalog, LastFMAsia, DeezerEurope), get_masks generates a GraphAny-style stratified split with 20 labelled nodes per class, rather than using an 'official' split.
findings.concern: The paper states it uses the datasets' 'respective official splits', but for the sizeable subset without predefined masks the splits are synthesised (a valid GraphAny-style protocol, just not the official one), so the description overstates split provenance.
findings.resolution: State which datasets use official splits vs a generated 20/class split; the generated procedure itself is fine, only the 'official splits' claim needs qualification.
findings.reason: Lines 46-52 of helpers/split_data.py match the quote; the else-branch at line 46 uses graphany_mask_splits with 20*num_class nodes when no predefined masks exist, contradicting the 'official splits' claim for those datasets.

findings.title: No CLI toggle for the 'plain' / 'no-bias' LS ablations (Tables 3–4)
findings.claim: The pool→label/feature LS operators (with a bias term `_b`) are always computed and always applied (equiv_layer.py:67-71). `ls_num_layers < 0` disables only the extra ls2x/ls2y layers, and there is no argument to remove the bias term. Tables 3–4 report 'plain' (no LS, no bias) and 'LS-only' (no bias) variants.
findings.concern: The exact ablation configurations in Tables 3 and 4 do not appear to be selectable through the provided CLI, so they may have required manual source edits — I could not confirm how they were produced.
findings.resolution: Authors: how were the 'plain' and 'no-bias' rows of Tables 3–4 generated — is there a flag or branch that disables the bias term and the pool-LS mixing?
findings.reason: Lines 106-112 of transforms/least_squares.py match the quote; equiv_layer.py:67-71 confirms the bias term is always applied, and grep on arguments.py finds no bias/plain/ablation toggle, supporting the claim.
